title: Foreign branch income — s 23AH ITAA 1936
summary: Facet map: is foreign branch income of a resident company exempt under s 23AH? Spine: resident company (not trustee — s 23AH(15)) → foreign PE in listed/unlisted country (s 23AH(2)) / capital gains on PE assets (s 23AH(3)-(4), not TAP) → ships/aircraft carve-out (s 23AH(14A)-(14B)) → hybrid mismatch (s 23AH(4A), (14C)-(14D)) → active income test (s 23AH(12)) → tainted exceptions (s 23AH(5) listed EDCI, (7) unlisted adjusted tainted income, (6)/(8) tainted assets) → disposal/interposition (s 23AH(9)-(11)). FACETS: AIT machinery and s 23AH(14) PE-company/HQ-company assumptions, adjusted tainted income and tainted assets (s 23AH(13)/(15)), listed vs unlisted countries (ss 320-321), hybrid mismatch detail (Div 832), definitions (s 23AH(15)). Subsection coverage: all of s 23AH(1)-(15) mapped. Rulings: TR 2014/3, TR 2002/5.

nodes.label: An Australian resident company derives foreign income (or a capital gain/loss) through a foreign branch — is it exempt under s 23AH?
nodes.body: Two paths under s 23AH: (1) foreign income derived through a foreign PE of a resident company is NANE (s 23AH(2)), subject to AIT/tainted-income exceptions (ss 23AH(5),(7)); (2) capital gains/losses on CGT assets used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE are disregarded (ss 23AH(3)-(4)) — that disregard is NOT conditioned on the AIT, but is denied for tainted assets (ss 23AH(6),(8)) and taxable Australian property (ss 23AH(3)(c),(4)(c)).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the taxpayer a resident company (not a trustee)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(15): 'company' does not include a company in the capacity of a trustee. The exemption is only for resident companies.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Not a resident company — s 23AH does not apply
nodes.body: s 23AH applies only to resident companies (s 23AH(15): company excludes trustee companies). Individuals, trusts and non-residents are outside this section. Resident individuals/trusts may rely on FITO (Div 770 ITAA 1997); non-residents are generally outside the Australian taxing base for foreign income unless specific source or anti-avoidance rules apply.

nodes.label: Is the foreign income, capital gain or capital loss derived in carrying on a business at or through a PE in a listed or unlisted country?
nodes.body: s 23AH(2): foreign income through a PE in a listed/unlisted country is NANE. ss 23AH(3)-(4): capital gains/losses on assets used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE are disregarded, unless the asset is taxable Australian property (ss 23AH(3)(c),(4)(c)) or tainted (ss 23AH(6),(8)). PE: DTA meaning if a DTA applies, otherwise the s 6(1) ITAA 1936 meaning (s 23AH(15)).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: No foreign PE — s 23AH does not apply
nodes.body: Foreign income is assessable with FITO relief (Div 770 ITAA 1997). TR 2014/3, TR 2002/5 explain PE.

rulings.title: carrying on a business at or through a permanent establishment
a place at or through which a person carries on any business

nodes.label: Is the foreign income, capital gain or capital loss from operating ships or aircraft in international traffic (or ancillary things)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(14A): the section does NOT apply to foreign income, capital gains or capital losses from operating ships/aircraft in international traffic (or things ancillary to that operation). s 23AH(14B): operates a ship/aircraft in international traffic = transporting passengers/goods by sea/air in the course of a business of operating ships/aircraft.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: International shipping/aircraft — outside s 23AH
nodes.body: Excluded (s 23AH(14A)). Often exempt under the DTA shipping article or subject to FITO.

nodes.label: Is there a branch hybrid mismatch (Div 832 ITAA 1997)?
nodes.body: s 23AH(4A): the exemption does not apply to branch hybrid mismatch income. s 23AH(14C): an amount is branch hybrid mismatch income to the extent it would give rise to a branch hybrid mismatch under Div 832. s 23AH(14D): PE in Div 832 takes the s 23AH meaning.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Branch hybrid mismatch income — not exempt
nodes.body: Assessable despite the PE (s 23AH(4A)).

nodes.label: Does the PE pass the active income test (s 23AH(12))?
nodes.body: Mirrors the CFC active income test in s 432, as modified by s 23AH(12): the PE passes if the entity would have passed s 432 on the s 23AH(14) assumptions and with ss 432(3), 446(2), 432(1)(b),(e) and 447(1)(b),(d),(f) treated as not enacted. Note: s 23AH(13) adjusted tainted income is used for the ss (5)/(7) tainted-income exceptions — NOT as the AIT pass measure.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: PE passes the AIT — income exemption applies
nodes.body: Foreign income is NANE (s 23AH(2)) — the AIT only matters for the tainted-income exceptions in ss (5)/(7). Capital gains/losses on the CGT path do NOT go through the AIT (see the CGT branch).

nodes.label: PE fails the AIT — check the country and tainted-income exceptions
nodes.body: AIT failure alone does not deny the exemption. For foreign INCOME: s 23AH(5) listed country — assessable only if the income is BOTH adjusted tainted income (s 23AH(13)) AND eligible designated concession income; s 23AH(7) unlisted country — assessable if the income is adjusted tainted income. For CGT assets, the tainted-asset rules are in ss 23AH(6)/(8) and apply regardless of the AIT (see the CGT branch).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Not adjusted tainted income — exemption applies despite AIT failure
nodes.body: The income is not adjusted tainted income (or not EDCI for listed countries) — the s 23AH(5)/(7) exceptions do not bite and the income remains NANE.

nodes.label: Income/gain assessable (exemption denied)
nodes.body: Exemption denied: ss 23AH(5)/(7) for foreign income (AIT failure + tainted amounts), ss 23AH(6)/(8) for capital gains/losses on tainted assets, or ss 23AH(3)(c)/(4)(c) for taxable Australian property. FITO (Div 770 ITAA 1997) may apply to residents.

nodes.label: s 23AH analysis complete
nodes.body: Foreign branch income is NANE unless: hybrid mismatch (4A), ships/aircraft (14A), AIT failure + tainted amounts (5)/(7), tainted assets (6)/(8), or taxable Australian property (3)(c).

nodes.label: FACET — AIT machinery: the s 23AH(14) assumptions
nodes.body: Where to look: s 23AH(12)-(14). The AIT is computed on assumptions isolating the PE: (a) only PE income counted (except for the 447(1)(a),(c),(e) and 450(6)(c),(7)(d),(8)(b) tainted-income paragraphs); (b) statutory accounting periods = years of income. s 23AH(13) adjusted tainted income feeds the ss (5)/(7) exceptions, not the AIT pass test.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Adjusted tainted income and tainted assets
nodes.body: Where to look: s 23AH(13) (adjusted tainted income = Part X adjusted tainted income on the s 23AH(14) assumptions, ignoring s 446(2) and 447(1)(b),(d),(f)); s 23AH(15) definitions (tainted asset, eligible designated concession income — Part X meanings). Listed-country CGT: gain/loss from a tainted asset is not disregarded only if it is also EDCI (s 23AH(6)); unlisted-country CGT: tainted asset alone denies the disregard (s 23AH(8)).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Listed vs unlisted countries (s 320 Part X)
nodes.body: s 320(1): listed country = a foreign country, or part of a foreign country, declared by the regulations; unlisted country = (a) a foreign country that does not (wholly or partly) consist of a listed country or countries, or (b) the remainder of a foreign country after its listed parts. Deeming rules for colonies/territories/protectorates in s 320(2)-(4). The listed/unlisted distinction drives which tainted-income exception applies (EDCI overlay for listed countries: ss 23AH(5)(c)(ii), (6)(b)).

statute.title: Listed countries

nodes.label: FACET — Branch hybrid mismatch (Div 832 ITAA 1997)
nodes.body: Where to look: Div 832 ITAA 1997 (hybrid mismatch rules — BEAP), s 832-575 (branch hybrid mismatch income), s 23AH(14C)-(14D). The s 23AH(4A) carve-out applies where a payment received by the company would otherwise give rise to a branch hybrid mismatch — the exemption is denied to the extent of the mismatch.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: FACET — Definitions (s 23AH(15))
nodes.body: s 23AH(15): company excludes trustee companies; double tax agreement has the Part X meaning; foreign income = an amount that (a) apart from this section would be included in assessable income under a non-CGT provision, AND (b) is derived from sources in a listed or unlisted country; PE in relation to a country = the DTA meaning if a DTA applies, otherwise the s 6(1) meaning; tainted asset and eligible designated concession income have the Part X meanings.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the amount derived from disposing of the business (s 23AH(9)) or through an interposed partnership/trust (ss 23AH(10)-(11))?
nodes.body: ss 23AH(9)-(11) are extension rules: s 23AH(9) treats income from disposing (in whole or part) of a business carried on at/through the PE as if derived in carrying on that business; ss (10)-(11) treat indirect interests through partnerships/trusts as derived through the company's own PE. They determine whether s 23AH applies at the outset — the same income/CGT analysis follows.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is this foreign income, or a capital gain/loss?
nodes.body: Foreign income follows ss 23AH(2),(5),(7) (AIT + tainted-income exceptions). Capital gains/losses follow ss 23AH(3)-(4) (asset-use, taxable Australian property, tainted asset) — the AIT is NOT applied to the CGT path.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Was the CGT asset used wholly or mainly for producing foreign income in carrying on a business at or through the PE?
nodes.body: s 23AH(3)(b)/(4)(b): required for the gain/loss disregard. If the asset was not used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE, the disregard is unavailable.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the CGT asset taxable Australian property?
nodes.body: s 23AH(3)(c)/(4)(c): the disregard does not apply to gains/losses on taxable Australian property (Div 855 ITAA 1997 concept).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the CGT asset a tainted asset (s 23AH(15), Part X meaning)?
nodes.body: Tainted assets deny the disregard: s 23AH(6) listed country (only if also EDCI), s 23AH(8) unlisted country (tainted asset alone suffices).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the PE in a listed or unlisted country?
nodes.body: Determines which tainted-asset rule applies: s 23AH(6) (listed: tainted AND EDCI) vs s 23AH(8) (unlisted: tainted alone).

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Is the gain/loss eligible designated concession income in relation to the listed country (s 23AH(6)(b))?
nodes.body: Listed-country tainted asset only denies the disregard if the gain/loss is also EDCI (Part X meaning). If not EDCI, the disregard still applies.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Listed country: is the foreign income BOTH adjusted tainted income AND eligible designated concession income?
nodes.body: s 23AH(5): listed-country income is assessable on AIT failure only if it is both adjusted tainted income (s 23AH(13)) and EDCI.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Unlisted country: is the foreign income adjusted tainted income?
nodes.body: s 23AH(7): unlisted-country income is assessable on AIT failure if it is adjusted tainted income (s 23AH(13)). No EDCI overlay for unlisted countries.

statute.title: Foreign branch income of Australian companies not assessable

nodes.label: Capital gain/loss disregarded (ss 23AH(3)-(4) apply)
nodes.body: The gain/loss is disregarded for Part 3-1 purposes: asset used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE, not taxable Australian property, and not a tainted asset (or tainted but not EDCI in a listed country).

nodes.label: Capital gain/loss NOT disregarded — assessable
nodes.body: Disregard unavailable: asset not used wholly/mainly for foreign income through the PE (s 23AH(3)(b)/(4)(b)), or taxable Australian property (s 23AH(3)(c)/(4)(c)), or tainted asset (ss 23AH(6)/(8)).

edges.label: Foreign income / capital gain or loss derived
No — no PE in a listed/unlisted country
No — not used wholly/mainly for foreign income
Yes — used wholly/mainly for foreign income
Unlisted country — tainted asset denies disregard
